page_convention: all pages are physical PDF page index (1-based)

test.question: For how long are institutions expected to keep records on gene therapy products and the trials that use them?
test.reference: Records about GTPs and their clinical trials have to be retained for no less than fifteen years, with the head of the institution supporting investigators in keeping them.
reference_claims: GTP and clinical trial records must be retained for at least 15 years

test.question: Above what construct size does a sponsor no longer have to sequence the whole vector, and what sequence must it supply instead?
test.reference: Vectors of 40 kb or smaller need full sequencing with an annotated sequence submitted; for anything larger, only the sequence of the active GTP component is required, alongside restriction maps.
reference_claims: Vectors up to 40 kb must be fully sequenced and annotated
For vectors above 40 kb, the sequence of the active GTP component must be provided

test.question: How long should trial participants who received a gene therapy product be followed up, and how long after marketing?
test.reference: Ideally participants are followed for at least five years, decided case by case, and a ten-year follow-up is recommended after the product is marketed.
reference_claims: Follow-up of at least 5 years (case by case) is recommended
Post-marketing follow-up of 10 years is recommended

test.question: What cleanroom grade is required for filling and packaging a gene therapy product, and is a lower grade allowed for bulk production?
test.reference: Final filling and packaging must happen in a Class A area; bulk manufacture may be done in either a Class B or a Class A facility.
reference_claims: Final filling and packaging must be done in a Class A area
Bulk production may be done in Class B or Class A

test.question: A CAR-T product has to be infused before final sterility results come back. On what basis can it be released, and who should be consulted?
test.reference: Because standard final sterility results would come too late, another sterility assurance approach is needed: release can rest on 24-48 hour culture sterility tests plus suitable molecular methods, worked out in consultation with GTAEC.
reference_claims: Release criteria may rely on 24-48 hour culture sterility tests
Appropriate molecular methods are used alongside
This is done in consultation with GTAEC

test.question: A dose cohort tolerated the product safely but did not get enough clinical benefit. Can those patients be dosed again with the same product, and what conditions apply?
test.reference: A second dose can be considered in that situation, but the same product is allowed only if there has been no local or systemic immune response over a reasonable follow-up of about one to two years; the immune data must be taken to GTAEC, and a GTAEC recommendation is mandatory for such protocol additions.
reference_claims: Yes: a second administration may be considered in this situation
The same GTP may be reused only if there is no immune response at the site or systemically over about 1-2 years
Immune response data must be evaluated and discussed with GTAEC
GTAEC recommendation is mandatory for such protocol additions or new applications

test.question: A developer has three candidates: an siRNA therapeutic, an autologous CAR-T cell product and a plasmid DNA vaccine. Which of these does the guideline cover, and does any carry further requirements?
test.reference: All three are covered: siRNA counts as a GTP, CAR-T cells are covered as ex vivo modified cells, and nucleic-acid DNA vaccines are covered too, though they will face additional requirements to be specified later.
reference_claims: siRNA products are GTPs under the guideline
CAR-T cells are GTPs (ex vivo genetically modified cells)
DNA vaccines (final product is nucleic acid) fall under the guideline
DNA vaccines carry additional requirements to be specified later

test.question: After the product has been given, how long must the patient stay in hospital under close watch, and to whom must adverse events in that period be reported straight away?
test.reference: Patients stay in hospital under close observation for at least 48-96 hours after administration, adjusted for the disease, product and expected serious events; all AEs and SAEs go immediately to the EC and CDSCO.
reference_claims: Patients must remain hospitalised under close observation for at least 48-96 hours after administration
All AEs and SAEs must be reported immediately to the EC and CDSCO

test.question: How often is the national gene therapy advisory committee expected to meet, and does its membership include anyone from outside science and government?
test.reference: It may meet every quarter, or more often if needed. Besides official nominees and biomedical experts, it includes ethics and legal experts, a social scientist, a lay person and a women's representative.
reference_claims: Meetings may be quarterly, or more frequent as needed
Membership includes non-scientific members such as a lay person, ethics/legal experts, a social scientist and a women's representative

test.question: The guideline forbids publicising GTP cures for diseases on a statutory list. Under which schedule of the drug rules is that list, and are genetic disorders on it?
test.reference: The list is Schedule J of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, reproduced in an annexure, and genetic disorders are one of the listed conditions, so GTP cure claims for them may not be advertised.
reference_claims: The list is Schedule J of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act/Rules
Genetic disorders appear on that list

test.question: When there is little experience with a product and its route, how should a first-in-human trial schedule its subjects, and how early must they be admitted before infusion according to the administration annexure that section points to?
test.reference: Consecutive subjects and the different dose cohorts should be staggered so that serious events can be watched and exposure limited; the annexure then requires first-in-human subjects to be admitted at least 24-48 hours before infusion.
reference_claims: Consecutively enrolled subjects should be staggered
Dose cohorts should also be staggered
First-in-human patients must be admitted no less than 24-48 hours ahead of the infusion

test.question: For a product already approved for clinical use abroad, what reduced preclinical testing may be enough, and when does that relief not apply?
test.reference: It may be enough to check just the clinical-grade vector lot against outcome measures within its release testing, but not if the delivery vector, the transgene or the production process has changed.
reference_claims: Testing may be limited to the clinical vector lot, checked against outcome measures within release testing
This does not apply if the delivery vector, transgene or production process varies

test.question: What fee does an applicant pay for a pre-IND consultation with the advisory committee?
test.reference: The guideline does not state this.
test.unanswerable_note: Pre-IND consultation is discussed (p6, p25, p88, p89) but no fee is set. Searched: 'fee' (only hit is 'feedback', p89); 'payment' (no hits); 'charge' (p3 'In-charge'; p25 'negatively charged'; p28 participants not liable to pay, PMS may be charged; p75 glossary; p95 tests free for participants). No fee for applicants anywhere.

test.question: Within how many days must the advisory committee give its recommendation on a clinical trial application?
test.reference: The guideline does not state this.
test.unanswerable_note: GTAEC review of trial applications is described (p25-26 s6.5, p89 s1.1.3, p104 flow) with no time limit. Searched: 'days' (no hits); 'timeline'/'time limit' (no hits); 'within' (p5, 8, 17, 27, 53, 75-77, 81, none a deadline); 'weeks'/'months' (only GMP batch duration, p46). Quarterly meetings (p89) are not a review deadline.

test.question: How is the compensation amount worked out if a participant dies because of a gene therapy trial?
test.reference: The guideline does not state this.
test.unanswerable_note: Out of scope: the compensation quantum comes from the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules 2019, which the guideline defers to (p28 s7.14). Searched: 'compensation' (only p98, a consent-template heading promising medical care for injury, no amount or formula); 'injury' (only p98); 'death' (only glossary 'mortality', p79). Also checked 'liab' (p28 s7.17/s7.19, p98): nothing on death compensation.

test.question: What membership must an institution's biosafety committee have? For example, is an outside expert or a DBT nominee required?
test.reference: The guideline does not state this.
test.unanswerable_note: Out of scope: IBSC constitution is governed by the Regulations and Guidelines on Biosafety of Recombinant DNA Research and Biocontainment 2017, which the guideline cites (p26 s6.2). Searched: 'IBSC' (p13, 26-28, 43, 45-46, 72, 104: approvals and duties only); 'composition'/'composed' (p25 and p89 refer to GTAEC; others unrelated); 'nominee' (only p89, GTAEC).

dev.question: How many rare diseases have Indian tertiary care hospitals reported so far, according to the guideline?
dev.reference: Tertiary hospitals in India have reported about 450 rare diseases.
reference_claims: About 450 rare diseases have been reported by tertiary care hospitals in India

dev.question: Which approvals does the model trial protocol expect the sponsor to document, and when is the stem cell committee included?
dev.reference: The protocol template lists approvals from the EC, RCGM, GTAEC and CDSCO, plus IC-SCR only when stem cells are used.
reference_claims: Approvals of EC, RCGM, GTAEC and CDSCO are listed
IC-SCR approval is needed only if stem cells are used

dev.question: What quorum is needed for the national gene therapy advisory committee to make a recommendation?
dev.reference: The guideline does not state this.
dev.unanswerable_note: GTAEC composition and meeting frequency are on p89; no quorum is given. Searched: 'quorum' (no hits); 'minimum number' (no hits); 'member' (p8, 26, 54, 89, 114: none states a quorum).
